I read through the whole path, from the microphone to the CLI and back. Here is what a turn actually costs today and what I would change.

## Where the time goes now

One spoken turn, first word out of the speakers:

| Step | Where | Rough cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Silence before the turn is called over | `gate.ts`, `CLOSE_MS = 620` | 620ms |
| Whisper transcribes, single threaded wasm, q8 | `listen.worker.ts` | 700 to 1500ms |
| **Git commit, pull and push before the CLI is even spawned** | `runner/index.ts:395`, `onBeforeRun` | 500ms to several seconds |
| Fresh `claude -p`, whole thread transcript rebuilt | `cli.ts`, `buildPrompt` | 1 to 3s |
| First full sentence before anything is said | `voiceReply.ts` | 200 to 800ms |
| Kokoro's first chunk, q8 wasm | `speak.worker.ts` | 600 to 1200ms |

That is four to ten seconds, and the middle two are the biggest and the least necessary. The streaming half is already right: text deltas arrive per token, `VoiceReply` releases per sentence, kokoro answers per sentence and `VoiceMouth` schedules them back to back. The waiting half is where everything is lost.

I also found two things that are plainly broken rather than slow, and one of them silences the conversation.

## Phase 1: take the waits out

**1. `src/shared/protocol.ts`** — add `voice?: boolean` to the `prompt` message, beside `ghost`.

**2. `src/server/session.ts`** — both `type: 'prompt'` sends (the resume sweep near 2431 and `runThread` near 2619) carry `voice: true` when the thread is a spoken one. The host already knows, `thread.voice` is right there.

**3. `src/runner/index.ts`** — `execute` skips `onBeforeRun` for a spoken turn. The 5 second loop still commits and pushes everything the agent does, so nothing stops syncing. What changes is that the first word no longer waits on a network round trip. The honest tradeoff: a spoken turn starts against what is on disk right now rather than after a pull. For a crew on one machine that is no difference at all, and for a crew across machines it is the same tree the last pass landed, seconds old.

**4. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/models.ts`** — a `backend(kind)` answering `{ device, dtype }`. WebGPU when `navigator.gpu` is there, the exact wasm settings there are today when it is not. Kokoro on WebGPU wants `fp32`, whisper wants an `fp16` encoder and a `q4` decoder. Electron 33 is Chromium 130, so WebGPU is there on every Mac this ships to, and a worker can reach it.

**5. `listen.worker.ts` and `speak.worker.ts`** — load through `backend()`, and if the WebGPU load or its first inference throws, load again on wasm rather than reporting a failure. This is the single largest win after the sync: whisper goes from over a second to a few hundred milliseconds, and kokoro goes from roughly real time to several times faster than real time, which is what makes a long answer stop stuttering between sentences.

**6. `src/main/index.ts`** — `app.commandLine.appendSwitch('enable-features', 'SharedArrayBuffer')` beside the three switches already there, and `env.backends.onnx.wasm.numThreads` from `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` in both workers. The wasm fallback is single threaded today because the page is not cross origin isolated. COOP and COEP headers would fix that too and would also break the GIF CDN and Google Fonts, so the switch is the way to do it.

**7. `src/renderer/src/state/voice.ts` and `src/renderer/src/App.tsx`** — a `warmVoice()` that loads both models and pushes 200ms of silence through whisper and one short phrase through kokoro with the audio dropped, called once from an idle callback when a session comes up, the way terminals are warmed. The first inference on any ORT session pays graph compile, two to five times the steady cost, and right now the person who pressed the mic pays it. Both workers get a `warm` message for this.

## Phase 2: the edges of a turn

**8. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/gate.ts`** — a fourth word, `pausing`, raised once per utterance at about 260ms of quiet. `CLOSE_MS` does not move, so nothing changes about when a turn is called over.

**9. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/ear.ts`** — `pausing` hands the audio so far to a new `onPause`, clearing nothing.

**10. `src/renderer/src/state/voice.ts`** — start whisper on the pause and remember the promise with the sample count it was made from. When the real end arrives at the same count, wait on that promise instead of starting again. If more sound arrived, drop it and transcribe the whole thing as now. On a normal turn the transcription is finished before the gate has even closed, which takes both the 620ms and most of the whisper time off the front.

**11. `src/shared/voiceReply.ts`** — the first release of a turn may end on a clause rather than a sentence, comma or colon or dash, once about sixteen characters are safe. Everything after it stays sentence granular. "Let me check," is a fine thing to say out loud and it lands most of a second earlier. `grew` already knows it is the first release from `this.at === 0`.

## Phase 3: barge-in, which is currently broken

Cut in on an answer while the run is still live and the follow up goes to `enqueuePrompt`, which sees `thread.running` and **steers the live run rather than starting a new one**. No `agent.start` is ever emitted for it, so `findTurn` in `turn.ts` matches nothing, forever. The orb sits on Working and the conversation never speaks again. This is the most common thing anyone does in a voice call and it kills the session.

**12. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/turn.ts`** — follow the message rather than the prompt text. Find the `message` event this window sent, then the `message.route` carrying its id, which gives the promptId for a queued turn and a steered one alike, and say which it was.

**13. `src/shared/voiceReply.ts`** — a `from(at)` so a reply adopted mid-run starts at the text already on screen rather than reading the first half of the old answer back out.

**14. `src/runner/providers/cli.ts` and `types.ts`** — `TURN_END_GRACE_MS` becomes a number the provider is handed, and a spoken turn gets about twenty seconds instead of 750ms. Once 12 is fixed this turns the whole thing around: the second turn of a conversation is a steer into a CLI that is still open, with its own context and a warm prompt cache, so there is no spawn and no transcript rebuilt. That is the difference between a two second turn and a sub second one, and it makes interrupting the fastest path rather than the broken one. The agent reads as busy to the crew for the length of the conversation, which is why the grace is bounded rather than open.

## Phase 4: say what it is doing

Everything needed is already arriving. Tool steps and thinking steps are in `crew.steps[promptId]`, `textOf` just filters them out, and `toolActions.ts` is already the one table that turns a tool name into "Reading" and "Ran".

**15. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/narration.ts`** (new) — steps to short spoken lines off that same table. The rules are what keep it from being a machine reading a log: never a path or a URL out loud, one line per tool, never the same line twice running so twelve file reads say "Reading files" once, at most one every few seconds, and nothing at all once the answer has started. Thinking gets the first sentence of the first thinking step only, and only if two seconds have gone by with nothing said, which is exactly what `--thinking-display summarized` gives on Claude and what Codex's per stretch headings give.

**16. `src/renderer/src/state/voice.ts`** — a `doing` on the state, and the line pushed into the mouth as an aside. It goes through the same kokoro stream, so ordering is free: narration only ever fires before there is answer text, so it is always said first, and a barge-in takes it with everything else.

**17. `src/renderer/src/components/voice/VoiceScreen.tsx`** — the standing line under the orb reads `doing` in place of "Working", which is worth doing on its own even with the spoken asides off, and a control in the bottom row toggles them.

**18. `src/renderer/src/media/voice/models.ts`** — `storedAsides` and `rememberAsides` beside the voice choice, so it is a setting and not a question each time. Default on.

## What holds it

- `tests/voice-listening.test.ts` for the new gate word and the hedge landing once per utterance
- `tests/voice-reply.test.ts` for the clause rule on the first chunk and for `from(at)`
- `tests/voice-turn.test.ts` for finding a turn through `message.route`, queued and steered
- `tests/voice-mouth.test.ts` for aside ordering and a barge-in taking them
- `tests/voice-narration.test.ts`, new, for steps to lines
- `tests/voice-thread.integration.test.ts` for a spoken prompt carrying `voice` and not waiting on the sync hook
- `yarn voice-check` reads the wasm dtype out of `models.ts` rather than hardcoding it, so the fallback stays covered. The WebGPU path cannot be seen from node and has to be checked in the app, which is the same rule the huddle has.

I would also have each turn print its four spans to the console in a dev build, heard, transcribed, first token, first word, so this gets tuned on numbers rather than on feel.

Phases 1 and 3 are where nearly all of it is. My estimate is first word in well under a second and a half on the first turn and under a second on every turn after, against four to ten seconds today.
